article.title: Bulk and scheduled sends
article.excerpt: Send to a list once, or at a future time, with per-batch pacing that protects your provider limits.

p: Two decisions shape a bulk send: which contacts are in it, and which channel carries it.
list: Adding contacts creates a batch, identified by a batch number. The batch is the unit you review and resend.
A batch sends over one channel that you pick — the whole batch goes through that single provider, with its sender numbers still rotating by weight inside it.
Pacing is applied per batch, so a large send does not exhaust the provider limits that your live traffic also depends on.

steps.p: Use a list, or import contacts by CSV. Numbers must be E.164.
Pick the batch and the channel it should send through, then write the content.
Immediate sends start as soon as you launch; a scheduled send waits for the time you set.
The batch view reports sent, failed, skipped and suppressed counts as it progresses.

sections.note: Scheduled sends are SMS-only today. If you schedule over another channel, the platform tells you rather than silently sending immediately.

p: Resending a failed batch retries only the recipients that were never attempted. Contacts that were already sent, or that are suppressed, are not sent to again — so a reset does not turn into a duplicate blast.

sections.h: Suppression counts as skipped, not failed
p: Recipients on the suppression list are counted separately from failures. A batch can therefore report a large skipped number and still be a healthy run — see "Opt-out and suppression" for why that is the correct outcome.
